# Project Overview

This project analyzes employee productivity, salary distribution, and project workload using **R** and **ggplot2**.  
The analysis includes data transformation, summary statistics, and visualization to uncover patterns in employee performance across departments.

## Environment Setup

This analysis uses the following R packages:

- **tidyverse** for data manipulation
- **ggplot2** for data visualization 
  
```{r loading packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```


### Creating dataset

```{r creating data frame, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
employee <- c("John", "Mary", "David", "Sarah", "Daniel", "Grace", "Michael", "Linda", "James", "Sophia")
department <- c("IT", "HR", "IT", "Finance", "IT", "HR", "Finance", "IT", "HR", "Finance")
experience <- c(3, 5, 2, 6, 4, 7, 3, 5, 4, 6)
salary <- c(4500, 5200, 4000, 6000, 4800, 6500, 4700, 5300, 5000, 6200)
project <- c(5, 6, 3, 7, 4, 8, 5, 6, 5, 7)
hoursworked <- c(160, 170, 150, 180, 165, 175, 160, 172, 168, 178)

employee_data <- data.frame(
  Employee = employee, Department = department,
  Experience = experience, Salary = salary,
  Project = project, HoursWorked = hoursworked
)
employee_data

```


### Transformation of Data

```{r}
employee_data <- employee_data %>%
  mutate(
    SalaryPerProject = Salary / Project,
    Productivity = Project / HoursWorked,
    Performance = ifelse(Project >= 7, "Excellent",
                         ifelse(Project >= 5 & Project <= 6, "Good",
                                "Average"))
  )
employee_data

employee_data$Employee <- factor(employee_data$Employee,
                                 levels = c("John", "Mary", "David", "Sarah", "Daniel", 
                                            "Grace", "Michael", "Linda", "James", "Sophia") )

```


### Summary Analysis

The following analysis calculates department-level statistics including average salary, maximum salary, employee count, and productivity.

```{r}
department_summary <- employee_data %>%
  group_by(Department) %>%
  summarise(AverageSalary = mean(Salary),
            MaximumSalary = max(Salary),
            MinimumSalary = min(Salary),
            TotalProject = sum(Project),
            Employeecount = n(),
            AvgProductivity = mean(Productivity))
department_summary
```


## Visualisation

### Salary by Department

```{r}
ggplot(data = employee_data, aes(x = Department, y = Salary, fill = Department)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "summary", fun = mean) +
    labs(
      title = "Average Salary By Department",
      x = "Department",
      y = "Salary"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
```


### Project Per Employee

```{r}
ggplot(data = employee_data, aes(x = Employee, y = Project)) +
     geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
     labs(
       title = "Number of Projects Per Employee",
       x = "Employee",
       y = "Number of Projects"
     ) +
     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```


### Salary vs Experience

```{r}
 ggplot(data = employee_data,
          mapping = aes(x = Experience,
                        y = Salary)) +
     geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +
     labs(
       title = "Salary vs Experience",
       x = "Experience",
       y = "Salary"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()
```


### Project vs WorkHours

```{r}
ggplot(data = employee_data, mapping = aes(x = HoursWorked, y = Project)) +
     geom_point(color = "darkgreen", size = 3) +
     labs(
       title = "Projects vs Hours Worked",
       x = "HoursWorked",
       y = "Projects"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()
```


### Salary Distribution

```{r}
 ggplot(data = employee_data, aes(x = Department,
                                    y = Salary, fill = Department)) +
     geom_boxplot() +
     labs(
       title = "Salary Distribution by Department",
       x = "Department",
       y = "Salary"
     )
```


## Key Insights

- The IT department shows a relatively higher average salary compared to other departments.
- There is a positive relationship between experience and salary, suggesting that employees earn more as they gain experience.
- Productivity levels vary across employees and departments.
- Some employees handle more projects with fewer working hours, indicating higher efficiency.
